headline: Revenue growth stays strong as losses narrow further
summary_short: GitLab's fiscal Q2 revenue rose 23.1% y/y to $264.2M, with the operating loss narrowing to $15.7M from $34.6M and net loss to $5.0M from $35.9M, even as gross margin slipped 2pp to 86% on rising SaaS hosting costs.
summary_long: Revenue growth was driven by new-customer additions, expansion within existing accounts, and growth in $100K+ ARR customers (1,519 vs 1,288 y/y), even as Dollar-Based Net Retention Rate slipped to 117% from 122%. Gross margin fell 2pp to 86% as third-party SaaS hosting costs rose faster than revenue. Operating expenses grew just 8% y/y (vs 23% revenue growth), driven by higher hosting and event costs in sales & marketing and headcount growth in R&D, narrowing the operating loss to $15.7M from $34.6M. Cash and short-term investments stood at $1,357.5M; GitLab repurchased $50.0M of stock this quarter ($350M remaining under its $400M buyback program) and generated $146.7M of adjusted free cash flow. No forward guidance is given in a 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Growth driven by new customer additions, expansion within existing accounts, and more customers surpassing $100K in ARR (1,519 vs 1,288 y/y); Dollar-Based Net Retention Rate was 117%, down from 122% a year ago.
Cost of revenue rose $12.5M, mainly $7.5M higher third-party SaaS/cloud hosting costs plus $3.8M higher personnel costs, outpacing revenue growth and cutting gross margin 2pp to 86% from 88%.
Revenue growth of 23% outpaced total operating-expense growth of 8% (higher S&M hosting/event costs and R&D headcount), narrowing the operating loss to $15.7M from $34.6M.
Not explained in the release — GitLab discloses no non-GAAP EBITDA reconciliation; this improvement mirrors the narrower operating loss for the quarter.

Net loss narrowed to $5.0M from $35.9M as the smaller operating loss was reinforced by a $10.2M swing to net other income (an FX loss last year vs a small FX gain this year) and a lower tax provision.
Tracks the narrower net loss; weighted diluted share count rose modestly to 169.9M from 164.5M, only partly offsetting the loss improvement.

MD&A frames the quarter as continued double-digit revenue growth funding operating leverage that narrowed losses, alongside $146.7M of adjusted free cash flow and a $50M share buyback, even as Dollar-Based Net Retention Rate eased to 117% from 122%.
